rows.backtranslation: Estimates include RAM for the current canvas and copied data, RAM for opening the image with fewer pixels, and RAM for editing. Actual RAM use varies. A smaller copy loses some details. The original file remains as it is.
rows.context_and_review_note: Made RAM for copied data explicit by repeating ⴷ RAM ⵏ, so the estimate does not syntactically combine a RAM quantity with data themselves. Copied data is a functional internal-clipboard paraphrase, not disk files. Retained estimates, variable actual use, fewer-pixel opening as sampled decoding rather than cropping, editing RAM, definite detail loss for a smaller copy and unchanged original file. Exact ImageResizeDialog.kt:34 selects this text only without native-work requirements. ImportPlan.create computes a power-of-two sample and decoded pixel estimate, then ImportedImage.decode uses that sample and scales/EXIF-transforms a bitmap to the target as needed. Sample can remain 1 for modest reductions, so wording is a description of sampled-resize working memory rather than a guarantee that every decode has fewer pixels. ImportPlan.estimatedBytes includes resident pixels and decoded/output editing reserves; ImportMemoryRequirements may add color metadata/wider decode storage. PaintDocument.residentPixels counts canvas, floating selection and internal bitmap clipboard. The explanation is not an exhaustive accounting claim or an allocation-success promise. Decode reads the original/private input and creates in-memory output; it does not overwrite the source file.

rows.backtranslation: Choose width and height. Neither may be greater than the corresponding original-image dimension.
rows.context_and_review_note: Retained direct width-and-height instruction and each corresponding original-dimension upper bound. Negative greater-than formulation permits equality and does not compare total pixel area. Exact ImportPlan.create requires target.width <= source.width AND target.height <= source.height and emits this string on failure. ImageResizeDialog.target applies the same per-axis bounds; positivity is separately enforced by ImageDimensions and need not be added here. No strict smaller-than or aspect-ratio requirement introduced.
